countingUnit: Japanese mora; explicitly authored hiragana readings. Small ya/yu/yo combine with the preceding kana; small tsu, n and long vowels count separately.

metricalExceptions.reason: Preserve the explicit affection and falcon species as natural Japanese. The first line is deliberately overlength; shortening falcon to hawk or removing lovely would lose a source fact. This is provisional extra-length verse, not a strict 5-7-5 pass; independent literary and special-scene acceptance remain pending.

semanticDecisions.reason: Assemble in linked order 504,581,580. Two beautiful women, a dashing male donkey and mating season. Equine is localized as the donkey present in this conversation; not a horse.
Rear gush, fluid along legs and wetting the earth remain explicit; the two quoted lines and the earth reaction use exactly the same Japanese verse wording.
Gentle licking cleans the speaker's mess and he becomes erect again. The implicit licking subject remains Violet from the surrounding dedication; the erection remains Oliver's.
The repeated poem ends in fortune for me; Violet changes the exact five-mora last line to fortune for everyone. Preserve singular versus collective rather than silently making both neutral.
Forever advancing, an endless journey and a flowing river remain. No invented seasonal image or stronger insight repairs Claire's underwhelmed response. Hiragana fixes the intended towa reading.
The little insect hurries about, followed by what matters to it and why now. Japanese ellipsis carries the busy activity into the last question; no invented wages or profession.
Earth is worked, raging water crossed and friends united; preserve the bridge interpretation and three distinct selectable slots.
